A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIX-versus-ORC weak-labeling study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including the two additional appendix sections in v2.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original simulations using 1,000 recordings per configuration, including synthetic event distributions and NIGENS-derived event lengths. Figures 6–12 present their outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and adds original analyses of NIGENS event timing and AudioSet weak-versus-strong annotations in Appendices A.4–A.5.

M1.justification: The FIX segmentation procedure, ORC construction from true boundaries, and deterministic event-fraction annotator model remain unchanged. The added analyses apply the existing framework rather than introduce another labeling method.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds evaluation of actual weak and strong AudioSet annotations for the Animal class, substantially extending coverage beyond simulated annotation and NIGENS-derived duration distributions. Appendix A.4 additionally uses observed NIGENS event timing; the original simulation coverage remains.

E2.justification: FIX and ORC remain the compared labeling approaches. The expanded discussion of adaptive change-point detection describes results attributed to Martinsson et al. (2024), without adding that method to this paper's evaluations.

E3.justification: The added NIGENS check fixes event duration to each class median and tests query lengths of 0.1, 1, and 10 times that duration. The AudioSet analysis averages per-event duration divided by the fixed 10-second query length and compares against Eq. 13. Existing simulation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a focused check of whether observed NIGENS event timing supports uniform relative offsets, examining three segment-to-event length ratios. The existing duration-distribution, event-density, and annotation-cost sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 adds indirect estimation of the annotator criterion by matching predicted accuracy to the AudioSet empirical mean. This estimate has no reported uncertainty interval; seed information and repeated-run uncertainty reporting remain absent.

E6.justification: v2 adds direct empirical evidence about real weak-label quality: Figure 20 reports AudioSet Animal accuracy of 0.162, matching the theoretical curve near gamma = 0.26. Figure 19 adds approximately uniform NIGENS offset distributions. These are new findings under additional conditions; the original simulation and cost results are retained.

T1.justification: Sections 2.1 and 4.2 revise the stated assumption from uniform event locations throughout a recording to local uniformity of event-query relative offsets. The five theorems, their expressions, and the proofs in Appendices A.1–A.3 remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusions retain the same claims about FIX accuracy limits, optimal segment length, annotation cost, and motivation for adaptive methods approximating ORC. The additional introductory summary restates these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications concerning stationary versus nonstationary sounds, independent annotation of overlapping classes, and conditions for transfer beyond audio. It also interprets the AudioSet comparison as empirical support, while Appendix A.5 acknowledges that proper validation requires independently estimating gamma from real annotators.

D1.justification: v1 refers to supplementary simulation code and promises a future repository link. v2 states that the code is openly released and supplies a concrete repository address for the simulations and symbolic verification notebook.

R1.justification: The introduction adds dataset examples such as SONYC, VGGSound, MATS, and YBSS-200. Section 7.1 adds Cheng et al. (2022) and Zhou et al. (2024) to distinguish modality-specific noise from temporal segment noise. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected introductory and modeling explanations and reorganizes the discussion into four thematic subsections. It also adds acknowledgments and changes author ordering and affiliations, while retaining the overall section structure and most technical prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 19–20 for the new appendix analyses, expands the Figure 4 caption, and regroups several existing figures across pages. The original plots and tables are retained, with publication headers added to the layout.

improvement.justification: The NIGENS timing check, AudioSet case study, clearer applicability conditions, and concrete code-access information modestly strengthen empirical grounding and usability. The gain is limited: the AudioSet gamma value is fitted to observed accuracy, and Appendix A.5 explicitly requires independent annotator measurements for proper validation despite stronger wording in Section 8. The central theory and simulation evidence remain unchanged.
